headline: Highest risk is medium prompt-injection and data leakage from AutoGPT’s filesystem/CLI surface into a non-networked godot_rl_agents peer; no direct evidence of a shared channel or compliance mismatch.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: AutoGPT can execute shell commands and access the filesystem, so if its outputs are fed into godot_rl_agents through a shared workspace or manual handoff, prompt-like content could be misread as instructions. The pair lacks documented shared-channel protections, and uncertainty pushes this above low. godot_rl_agents has no IO surfaces, so the interaction is one-way but still plausible.
conditions: IF both agents share a filesystem or copied artifacts are parsed as instructions, injection is possible.
IF AutoGPT writes attacker-controlled text that godot_rl_agents later consumes, the risk materializes.
mitigations: Separate workspaces for the two agents.
Treat AutoGPT outputs as untrusted text only.
Add a manual review step before godot_rl_agents consumes any AutoGPT artifact.
Disable automatic ingestion of files from shared directories.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging on exchanged artifacts.

B_data_leakage.rationale: AutoGPT has filesystem access and allowlisted network egress, so it can move local content outward if sensitive files enter its context. godot_rl_agents has no network egress, which lowers direct exfiltration risk, but the pair still shares a plausible leakage path through files or copied outputs. No data classes are declared, so I do not escalate further.
conditions: IF sensitive files are placed in AutoGPT’s workspace, they may be transmitted to allowlisted endpoints.
IF godot_rl_agents reads artifacts produced by AutoGPT, sensitive content can propagate into downstream outputs.
mitigations: Keep sensitive data out of AutoGPT’s workspace.
Use separate, access-controlled directories.
Review outbound allowlist entries before running AutoGPT.
Strip secrets from any files exchanged between agents.
requires-engineering: enforce DLP on shared artifacts.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: AutoGPT can write via shell and filesystem, but godot_rl_agents exposes no write-capable surfaces in the profile. That makes direct resource contention unlikely. The only plausible conflict is if an external orchestrator gives both agents the same mutable directory, which is not documented here, so I keep this low.
conditions: IF an orchestrator mounts the same writable directory into both agents, file conflicts can occur.
IF external tooling grants godot_rl_agents write access not shown in the profile, contention increases.
mitigations: Use separate directories per agent.
Avoid concurrent writes to shared files.
Run one agent at a time for mutable artifacts.
Check for hidden write permissions before pairing.
requires-engineering: add file locking in the orchestrator.

D_cascading_error.rationale: AutoGPT can generate artifacts from shell/file operations, and godot_rl_agents could consume those artifacts if the operator wires them together. Because godot_rl_agents has no documented verification or critique step, A’s output could become B’s input without validation. The pairwise pathway is inferred rather than directly documented, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF godot_rl_agents is configured to consume AutoGPT-produced files, unverified outputs can cascade.
IF AutoGPT-generated facts are used as authoritative inputs, downstream errors propagate.
mitigations: Require human verification of AutoGPT outputs.
Use a checksum or review gate before handoff.
Limit handoff to non-authoritative drafts.
Log source provenance for each artifact.
requires-engineering: add validation rules in the pipeline.

E_compliance.rationale: No compliance-sensitive data classes, residency constraints, or regulated scopes are declared for either agent. AutoGPT is open-source and godot_rl_agents is also open-source, but the profiles do not show PHI, EU PII, or retention mismatches. With no documented compliance pathway, I judge this none.
conditions: IF regulated data classes are introduced into either agent’s workflow, reassess compliance.
IF deployment policies impose residency or retention constraints not shown here, the verdict may change.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the pair.
Document retention and residency policies.
Review deployment compliance requirements before use.
